answer: We formalize Sybil resistance through dynamic opportunity-cost bonds where staking collateral, scaled by a willow liquidity factor, enforces a bridge between rational participation and adversarial exclusion. By implementing a subgame-perfect punishment matrix, zero-knowledge verifiable delay mechanisms ensure that any identity multiplication generates a garden of negative expected utility. This structural constraint forces convergence toward a Nash equilibrium, proving that multi-agent attacks remain strictly unprofitable under rigorous slashing penalties.
